entities.summary: Dame Jilly Cooper was an English author and journalist, best known for her long-running Rutshire Chronicles series. She began her career in journalism and published several works of non-fiction, including books on class, animals and marriage, before turning to fiction. Her first book was How to Stay Married, which was published in 1969. She published several collections of journalism, alongside other non-fiction volumes throughout much of her career. Cooper's first novel to be published was the romance Emily, which appeared in 1975 and was followed by five more, as well as a volume of short stories.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jilly Cooper's Rutshire Chronicles series was a best-selling and influential work of English literature, contributing to the development of rural fiction in the UK. Her writing had a notable impact on the genre, with her works being widely read and adapted into film and television.
